newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Short sterling vols up, focus on rates.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Short sterling vols up, focus on rates.

text.p: Calls from Bank of England Governor Eddie George for a "modest pre-emptive" monetary tightening pushed up implied volatility levels of options on short sterling futures on Tuesday, traders said.
A rise in interest rates could take place after the next monthly meeting between George and Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, to be held on February 5.

"We have seen buyers of put spreads and buyers of puts," said a broker at a U.S. bank in London. "People still believe rates will still be raised so they want to cover themselves against that eventuality."
Implied volatility on short sterling options was quoted at 9.0 percent middle for March and 11.30/12.20 percent for June, compared with 8.21 percent and 11.14 percent respectively on Tuesday.

LIFFE data showed around 2,800 lots of puts at the March 93.50 strike had been traded and more than 7,000 lots at the 93.75 strike. Similar numbers of calls had also been traded at those strikes and around 3,000 lots at the 94.00 strike.
In June options, around 2,500 lots of the 92.75 put and 1,000 lots of the 93.25 put had also changed hands.
The underlying March short sterling future was trading at 93.59, down one basis point on the day at 1428 GMT.
Elsewhere in the options market, brokers said volatility on Euromark options was little changed but may hold a bit firmer until after the Bundesbank monetary meeting on Thursday.
"A bullish combo (combination trade) has gone through on December but that is about all," a LIFFE trader at a British Bank said.
Gilt options had also seen some activity in the March contract -- particularly buying of March 113.00 calls, he said.
The February gilt serial options expire on Friday.
